Concept role: dwp:DecisionRule.","text":"Source-bounded Pension Credit research through DMG 077001–077004, not a rule for all benefits. Other entitlement conditions must continue. The captured four-week branch requires an absence not expected to exceed four weeks; the examples distinguish expected duration from an early return or later extension. The eight-week branch requires the specified death connection, an absence not expected to exceed eight weeks and the Secretary of State considering return within four weeks unreasonable. The twenty-six-week branch requires an absence not expected to exceed twenty-six weeks and solely for the specified treatment, medically approved convalescence or care, or accompanying the specified person. Preserve the practitioner, pre-existing-condition and accompanying-person qualifications exactly as stated on pages 9–11; being abroad when an accident occurs is not itself the stated purpose condition. The qualified-practitioner definition continues onto page 11. Household membership, qualifying young person, the dated 2016 transition and the source-described non-export boundary need separate conditional review. Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Introduction\n\n077001 SPC can continue to be paid whilst a claimant is temporarily absent from GB 1 if the other\nconditions of entitlement continue to be satisfied and the absence is no longer than\n\n\n1. 4 weeks where the absence is not expected to exceed 4 weeks2 or\n\n\n2. 8 weeks3 where paragraph 077002 applies or\n\n\n3. 26 weeks4 where paragraph 077003 applies.\n\n\nNote: See DMG 04642 for effective dates for supersession.\n\n\n                                                 1 SPC Regs, reg 3; 2 reg 3(1)(a); 3 reg 3(1)(b); 4 reg 3(1)(c)\n\n\nExample 1\n\n\nJason notifies the DM that he is going abroad for 3 weeks. The DM decides that he remains entitled for\nthose 3 weeks. He contracts food poisoning and has to extend his stay by a further 2 weeks. As Jason’s\n\nperiod abroad was not expected to exceed 4 weeks the DM decides that he remains entitled for 4 weeks\nbut supersedes and disallows for the 5th week.\n\n\nExample 2\n\n\nNicola notifies the DM that she will be going abroad for 5 weeks. The DM supersedes and disallows from\nthe beginning of the absence. Due to unforeseen circumstances Nicola returns after 3 weeks. However\nNicola’s award remains disallowed as the absence was expected to last more than 4
